transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-08 15:00 UTC | Duration: 45m
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Rourke (Redwood SE), Daniel Park (CTO - Vectora), Rina Kapoor (Eng Mgr), Sanjay Patel (DevOps)

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Maya, I'm the AE on this account, and with me is Liam our solutions engineer. Quick agenda \u001F understand your quickstart needs, talk through hosted vs dedicated/private, and next steps for a PLG sandbox.
[00:23] Daniel: Yeah thanks, we appreciate you fitting us in. Quick context \u001F Vectora's building a developer chat assistant embedded in our analytics UI. Priorities are low latency for short chat, and easy onboarding for our product team. We were looking at OpenAI, Replicate, and saw Redwood from the benchmarks.
[00:45] Liam: Awesome, thanks for that. Can you share current stack real quick? Are you on k8s in AWS, any VPC constraints, data residency?
[00:55] Rina: We run EKS in us-west-2, some services in GCP but core infra is AWS. We do have strict compliance for customer data, must be able to keep logs internally, and SSO is via Okta.
[01:08] Maya: Good \u001F that's a common setup. For PLG/self-serve the usual path is onboard to Redwood hosted API, we give free credits and a quickstart org so engineers can get to first token in minutes. If you need, we can later map to Dedicated or Private with VPC peering.
[01:30] Sanjay: When you say first token in minutes, how does that work? Do we need to install anything?
[01:36] Liam: No heavy install. For hosted you create an org, we provision API keys; SDKs in JS/Python, one line to run. Time-to-first-token depends on you \u001F but front-to-back we typically see devs making a call in under 10 minutes with the quickstart. There is a CLI too.
[01:55] Daniel: Sounds good. Two concerns \u001F latency and cost. We need sub-200ms for token generation for short replies. Also cost at scale matters. How do you trade off hosted vs dedicated?
[02:12] Liam: Right \u001F hosted is simplest and quickest. For latency-sensitive workloads you can use Dedicated (reserved GPU pools) or Dedicated with colocated regions. Dedicated gives more predictable p99s and lower tail latency, but it's a commitment (monthly). Hosted can be very competitive with routing policies and warm KV cache but tails can vary. For cost, Redwood Optimize suggests quantization and batching for throughput workloads.
[02:40] Rina: We might start with hosted to validate product-market fit and then move to dedicated if latency/regulatory needs arise. For security, what certifications do you have? SOC 2?
[02:52] Maya: We are SOC 2 Type II and have ISO on the roadmap. We also support SSO via SAML/Okta, RBAC in the Console, audit logs, and KMS integrations for Private deployments. I'll send our security whitepaper and SOC 2 report token.
[03:10] Daniel: Great. About data retention \u001F can we configure logs retention and is there an option to prevent storage of customer payloads?
[03:18] Liam: Yes, you can set retention windows per org; for Private and Dedicated you get stronger controls and optional disabling of persistent logs. For hosted, we have configurable retention and options for enterprise customers.
[03:32] Sanjay: If we move to Private, how does networking look? VPC peering? On-prem?
[03:38] Maya: For Private we support a customer-managed control plane, VPC peering, and an on-prem package if needed. There is some setup work on the infra side; Liam can scope network requirements.
[03:50] Liam: I'll send a short checklist \u001F required ports, subnets, and KMS configuration. Also, if you want to run latency benchmarks we can provide a lightweight harness and recommended model variants.
[04:05] Daniel: Speaking of models, what do you surface in the catalog \u001F open models or Redwood-optimized variants?
[04:12] Liam: We host a curated catalog: open models with Redwood-verified performance profiles, and we offer model variants for latency/cost tradeoffs, e.g., quantized 4-bit options. We also support streaming responses and function calls for structured outputs.
[04:28] Rina: Any gotchas on tokenization/embedding consistency? We use embeddings for similarity search.
[04:34] Liam: Embeddings are supported, and you can pin model versions. We'll share embedding quality benchmarks; note that small differences in tokenization can affect cosine distances \u001F we include migration docs.
[04:50] Maya: Quick question for you \u001F who's owning the integration and what's your timeline?
[04:55] Daniel: Rina and Sanjay will own implementation; goal is POC in 3 weeks and a pilot in 8 weeks. If the quickstart goes well we want to onboard product engineers immediately.
[05:08] Maya: Great. We'll issue free credits for a 7-day sandbox and a quickstart guide with sample code to get you to first token.
[05:16] Rina: Can you show a quick demo of the one-line call?
[05:20] Liam: Sure \u001F opening my screen (note: demo just described). Example JS snippet: const client = new RedwoodClient(process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY); const res = await client.chat.create({model: 'redwood-chat-1', messages: [{role:'user', content:'summarize sales notes'}]}); console.log(res.choices[0].message.content);
[05:45] Rina: Nice. What about streaming for UI?
[05:48] Liam: We support streaming via SSE and websockets in the SDKs; that helps reduce time-to-first-token perceived by users.
[05:56] Sanjay: For benchmarks, what should we measure? p50, p95, p99? And sequence length?
[06:02] Liam: Measure p50/p95/p99 and tail; include concurrency and typical sequence lengths. For short chat we're usually looking at 32-64 tokens per response. We'll share a template and run a joint run if you want.
[06:20] Daniel: On SLAs \u001F for hosted trial there's none; for Dedicated we can talk SLA and uptime targets.
[06:28] Maya: Correct, hosted public tier has standard uptime and best-effort; Dedicated includes SLA-backed uptime and latency targets.
[06:35] Rina: Cost model \u001F how does pricing show up during the trial? Is it per-token? Any flat fees?
[06:42] Maya: Hosted is usage-based (per token / per-embedding). No flat fee for the sandbox; Dedicated involves reserved capacity contracts. We'll send a simple pricing sheet so you can model costs.
[06:55] Sanjay: Anything we should be careful about with rate limits during the quickstart?
[07:00] Liam: We give generous sandbox quotas; if you hit limits we'll temporarily raise them. For production, there are per-route quotas and rate limiting with graceful backpressure.
[07:12] Daniel: Ok helpful. A couple notes: we run extra compliance checks \u001F can you provide pen test summary and SOC2 attestations?
[07:20] Maya: Yes I'll include pen test summary and SOC 2 artifacts in the security packet.
[07:28] Rina: How do rollouts work if we change models mid-pilot? Canary? A/B?
[07:34] Liam: Redwood supports canary deploys, A/B, and automatic fallback policies. You can pin model versions and set rollout percentages in the Console.
[07:45] Daniel: Good. Any integration with our logging stack? We use Datadog and S3 for long-term logs.
[07:52] Liam: We integrate with Datadog and you can stream audit logs to S3 for retention.
[08:00] Maya: Quick recap then: we'll send quickstart guide, sandbox creds and free credits, security docs (SOC2/pen test), and a sample benchmark plan. Liam will scope the latency test and send network checklist. Sanjay will send infra diagram.
[08:18] Sanjay: I'll get that over by Friday.
[08:22] Daniel: Let's plan the benchmark call for 9/14.
[08:26] Maya: Sounds good \u001F I'll schedule and invite Liam. Anything else?
[08:30] Rina: One last question \u001F do you support customer-managed keys for hosted?
[08:34] Liam: Customer-managed KMS is available for Private; for Hosted we offer integration options for enterprise tiers. We'll clarify which tiers support CMK in the security doc.
[08:45] Daniel: Perfect. Thanks everyone.
[08:48] Maya: Thanks, we'll follow up with the artifacts today.
[08:52] (call ends)

Notes on transcription: Some words may be auto-transcribed (e.g., KV cache pronounced as "K V cash" at one point), name spellings might be off in raw export. Action items recorded above.
